pages.text: Delegation pins one mage to one building. The Item Workshop, Equipment Workshop, Magic Workshop and Element Node panels each carry a Delegate button in their lower right corner — press it and pick a mage.
$(bold)The Three Rules$()$(li)That mage works $(bold)only on this building$(): it takes no other building's jobs, and no job that belongs to no building either (guarding, altar casting).

This building's jobs go $(bold)only to that mage$(): while it is busy, following you, or too far away, the job waits in the queue instead of going to someone else.$(li)$(bold)A mage serves one building at a time$(): delegating it to another building moves it off its old post.

Press Delegate to open the mage list. Each row says what that mage is doing right now (Idle / Working / Following a player), and a row already assigned somewhere else names that building — clicking it moves the mage here.
pages.title: How to Use It

pages.text: To put the building back to "any mage may take its jobs", open the list again and press Clear Delegation.$(br2)$(bold)When It Pays Off$()

Assign a mage when you want one workshop to keep working, or a node to keep producing, without other buildings stealing the worker.$(br2)Be careful in a small town: a delegated mage takes no guard jobs and will not help with construction, so one post locks up one mage.

The mage $(bold)does not teleport$() — it walks there. If the mage's chunk is not loaded, this building's jobs keep waiting for it.$(li)A change is $(bold)not instant$(): a job already running is returned to the queue on the next tick and picked up again right away, restarting from its material-fetch step.
pages.title: Things to Know

pages.text: If the mage dies or is dismissed, the delegation is released and the building takes any mage again. A chunk unload does $(bold)not$() release it — the mage comes back, so the post is kept.$(li)Demolishing or undoing the building takes the delegation with it.
